description.narrative: Stöd för att konsolidera den albanska statliga polisens strategi för att bättre betjäna de lokala samhällena och deras säkerhets- och säkerhetsprioriteringar i samarbete med lokala myndigheter och organisationer i det civila samhället.

Support to consolidate the Albanian State Police approach towards serving better the local communities and their security and safety priorities in cooperation with local governments and civil society organizations.

The aim of the programme remains the same as in the previous phase: Improved trust and partnership between police and community contributes towards safer neighbourhoods.
The intervention has been built on three main pillars pillars which are considered mutually necessary in supporting sustainable improvements:
1) improving the effectiveness of implementation of community policing. The first pillar focuses on consolidating and expanding on the ASP adoption of community policing as an approach. This will involve managing any processes of ASP structural change to ensure that gains in community policing approaches are maintained, improving consistency of implementation of community policing across the country and further training of staff in community policing principles.
2) strengthening the police state accountability and coordination along with the community policing analysis capability.The second pillar continues to develop a data driven approach to community policing across the ASP, while strengthening linkages between the parts of government with a remit for ensuring public safety. In doing this it ensures that the ASP makes decisions on the basis of a strong understanding of community priorities, and is capable of leveraging the full range of government capabilities in support of improving community safety;
3) improving police responses to community priorities, including domestic violence. The final pillar focuses on ensuring that the ASP have adequate capacity in the key speciality policing topics of domestic violence, traffic, and youth engagement. This pillar ensures that ASP responses to community priorities are appropriate and grounded in a strong understanding of the issues, the needs of vulnerable groups, and that the police have the appropriate capabilities to provide an adequate response.
Finally, as in the previous phases, grants scheme for the civil society organizations will be used to reinforce reforms and improve community engagement by linking and funding relevant CSOs to influence the reforms that are being implemented internally. Possible areas of intervention through the grant scheme should be considered and decided by the Programme Steering Committee (PSC). The initial priorities of the Grants Scheme will be to reinforce LCPS by enabling active and informed community participation and to ensure that community policing is well engaged with motivated community groups representing the range of key stakeholders (at minimum women, youth) in advocacy, municipality and zone level relationship building. By funding small forms of direct support to CSO efforts on community concerns, the CSOs will be able to attend LCPS meetings with an informed sense of actual community issues.
The expected results of the intervention are:
1) Police effectively implement community focused approaches
2) Police are well integrated into municipal community safety councils
3) Police respond to community priorities
Each result is broken down in outputs that could directly contribute to its achievement.

During the 2025 the intervention has trained jointly 449 Albanian State Police (ASP) general patrol officers, CommandandControl Rooms and Information Offices staff on community policing, which enhanced their internal cooperation in managing incidents, through mutual understanding of duties, responsibilities and capabilities. Another result of training was increased self reliance of the trainees in daily routine operations, without depending on continuous advice and supervision from superiors. In cooperation with civil society, the training equipped the police with better capacities to Counteract Violent Extremism, as a new topic for their on the job preparation. The managerial staff of 4 police commissariats and 3 police stations in four different municipalities were enabled to evaluate better the functionality of police zones and analyze public order statistics, through coaching from the programme staff. A revision of the analyzable and meaningful set of data to be collected regularly from the police in order to assess their own organizational performance, was carried out, resulting in a new regulation for data reporting that is more advanced and usable for follow up and decisio nmaking. In seven municipalities the Local Councils for Public Safety (LCPS) have been coached to increase their performance as facilitators of evidence-based dialogue between communities, local authorities, and police structures. Coupled with implementation of the Local Safety Measurement System (LSMS) for the same municipalities, this has improved the targeting of local safety needs of the different actors, including the police. A thoroughly revised Standard Operating Procedures for handling Domestic Violence (DV) cases incorporating procedural updates of April 2025, has been finalized to strengthen protection mechanisms, enhance the prevention of violence against women across a broad spectrum of gender-based violence, including online harassment, stalking, and psychological abuse. Over the reporting period, 18 awareness-raising events against DV engaged women from rural and suburban communities, as well as students in schools across the targeted municipalities. Awareness was raised about digital violence against women through a dedicated multiple stakeholders event. Students from 12 schools raised their awareness through information and practical simulation sessions on safe road behavior through interactive learning methods. The messages were further disseminated through social and local media platforms, regarding key road safety topics like seat belt use, speed limits, and responsible driving habits. Dozens of young activists and volunteers were trained and mobilized to support the implementation of these activities ensuring sustainability and community ownership. The Albanian Police have now a comprehensive pool of well-trained Community Policing Officers, capable of enhancing youth safety and preventing antisocial behavior within school environments in the whole country and developing School-Police partnerships. This is part of the National Action Plan for Strengthening Mechanisms to Prevent All Forms of Violence and Bullying for Safety in Pre-University Educational Institutions, 20252027, implemented by the State Police, resulting in standardized community police engagement in educational settings. Through interactive training workshops on Cybercrime and Cyberbullying, 40 Community Policing Officers assigned as Youth Educators increased their knowledge of online security, were enabled to address real cases, and strengthened their capacity to inform and raise awareness among youth in schools and communities about digital risks. Through the Grants scheme, the intervention has further strengthened the partnership between civil society organizations, and the police, schools and local governments in different regions of Albania. The programme is well on track to deliver towards its main objectives. There are several training packages developed from the intervention and endorsed and incorporated in the ASP regular capacity building programmes for different types of police officers, about community policing concepts and practices. Further, revised handbooks for Community Policing Officers (CPO) youth educators are distributed to all CPO youth educators as well as to the Community Policing Sector at the Albanian State Police. The handbooks are currently aligned with contemporary community contexts and provide practical, actionable guidance for engaging diverse age groups, schools, and local organizations. Due to the efforts of the Community Policing Phase 3 intervention, education and awareness in schools remain a key pillar of community policing, supporting long-term safety, social cohesion, and youth engagement across Albania. The intervention has also increased the evidence-based decision making at ASP through a variety data collection methods like Police Satisfaction Surveys (every two years), LSMS, LCPS, and has refreshed the standards operating Procedures for DV cases. The building of partnership with civil society, schools and local governments has progressed steadily and is being further institutionalized. The Community Policing Programme remains highly anchored into the main Albanian counterparts, ASP and the Ministry of Interior. It is also developing collaboration with the new bilateral project of cooperation between the Swedish and Albanian Police authorities in the area of DV. Sida assesses that the intervention is delivering and contributing sustainable towards the stated objectives. There are no new or stronger risks associated with the intervention and the already identified ones have been mitigated to the extent possible (like lower engagement during elections period and change of staff at ASP).
